slot.brief: Find the equation of the line through the intersection point of two given lines and passing through an external point, using the family L1 + λL2 = 0.

stem: The equation of the line through the intersection of $x+2y-8=0$ and $2x-y-1=0$, and the point $(5,1)$, is

verdicts.working: Solving the two equations gives intersection (2,3). The line through (2,3) and (5,1) is 2x+3y-13=0.

working:
The two lines intersect at $P=(2,3)$. The family is $(x+2y-8)+\lambda(2x-y-1)=0$. Substituting $(5,1)$ gives $-1+8\lambda=0$, so $\lambda=\dfrac{1}{8}$. Thus $8(x+2y-8)+(2x-y-1)=0$, or $2x+3y-13=0$.

Independent check: Solving the two equations gives intersection (2,3). The line through (2,3) and (5,1) is 2x+3y-13=0.
solution:
Solving the two equations gives their intersection $P=(2,3)$. The line through $P$ and $(5,1)$ is
$$\frac{x-2}{5-2}=\frac{y-3}{1-3}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad 2x+3y-13=0.$$
